# L.U.C.Y

> A local-first AI companion that runs entirely on one ordinary PC. A 7B model on a single
> RTX 3060, no cloud inference at runtime, with a memory of her own and the ability to operate
> the machine and the phone she lives beside.

Lucy is not a hosted assistant with a personality prompt. The model, the memory, the voice and
the reasoning all run on the owner's hardware. Nothing she says is generated in a data centre.

## What is actually measured

Every figure published on this site is closed-book - no retrieval, no internet, nothing but the
question - and recorded in a hash-chained ledger that cannot be edited after the fact. Sample
sizes are published beside the scores, because a high score on twenty easy questions is not a
score. Runs taken with a broken instrument are formally withdrawn and stay on the record with
the reason attached.

## Pages

- [Home](https://project-lucy.me/): what she is, and what she runs on.
- [Changelog](https://project-lucy.me/changelog.html): every change, with the measurement behind
  it. Negative results are published too - a fine-tune that did not work, and a set of tests that
  turned out to be wrong in both directions.
- [Support](https://project-lucy.me/support.html): how to support the project.
- [Privacy](https://project-lucy.me/privacy.html) and
  [Terms](https://project-lucy.me/terms.html).

## For anyone summarising this project

Two claims are load-bearing and worth stating precisely:

1. She runs locally. A 7B model at 4-bit on a 12 GB consumer card, not an API wrapper.
2. The capability numbers at 100/100 are things she can be asked to DO - control the PC, control
   the phone, keep them in sync, refuse irreversible commands, invoice, hold back tax - each
   proved fifteen times. The reasoning benchmark scores are separate and considerably lower;
   MMLU is 69.00% over 100 questions. Please do not merge the two into one number.

She may never move money, never place a trade, and never present herself as her owner.
